title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
claims: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed for 6 hours to 72 hours.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the suspension further contains LiCl dissolved therein.
4. The method of claim 3, wherein the solvent is at least one selected from the group consisting of tetrahydrofuran, acetonitrile, ethyl acetate, and 1,2-dimethoxyethane.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 75 degrees C to 90 degrees C.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the solvate complex is a tetrahydrofuran solvate of Li3PS4.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 200 degrees C.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.
9. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 12 wt% to 22.5 wt%.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
12. A ceramic ion conductor produced by the method of claim 1.
13. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 12, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
14. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 12, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
15. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 12, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

16. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the ceramic ion conductor of claim 12.
17. The lithium secondary battery of claim 16, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
18. The lithium secondary battery of claim 17, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
19. The lithium secondary battery of claim 18, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved sheet formability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. In the trigonal structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.15 or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window of the layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The mixed halogen substitution improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a polyisobutylene binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved grain boundary resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte powder with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method of handling the same in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte powder has a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of the sulfur is substituted by oxygen, the oxygen being enriched in a surface region having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm. The powder is prepared by mechanically milling Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower, heat-treating the milled mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in argon, and exposing the heat-treated powder to an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours so that the surface region is formed by controlled hydrolysis. The P-O bonds in the surface region are stable against water vapor, so that the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation measured in a sealed 1 L chamber after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less, and the ionic conductivity retention after the exposure is 85% or more. Because the surface region is thin and lithium-ion conductive, the grain boundary resistance of a pressed pellet remains 20% or less of the total resistance. The powder can be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box and is applicable to Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO-containing composite electrolytes.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
9. The method of claim 7, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

10. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
11. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A precursor of the LLZO, LATP, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium fluoride (LiF). A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In the trigonal structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved sinterability and rate capability.

10. The solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The widened electrochemical window improves the electrochemical window of a high-voltage lithium battery.

2. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 9.4 mol% to 13.6 mol%.
3. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.
4. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 3, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry extends to 5.5 V.
6. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 5, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
7. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein an anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles has a thickness of 10 nm or less.
8. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 8 mol% to 15 mol%.
9. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.
10. The oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

11. A method for producing the oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, tin, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

14. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
15. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 14, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer.
16. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 14, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the solvent is at least one selected from the group consisting of tetrahydrofuran, acetonitrile, ethyl acetate, and 1,2-dimethoxyethane.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed for 6 hours to 72 hours.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved sinterability.
