title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The resulting LLTO and LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The LLTO and LATP material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The LATP and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. A solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. With hafnium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. With hafnium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved interfacial resistance.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the cycle life at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sheet formability.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.1 wt% or less.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 530 degrees C to 580 degrees C.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more.

10. The ion-conductive solid of claim 9, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
11. The ion-conductive solid of claim 10, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.

12. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the ion-conductive solid of claim 9.
13. The all-solid-state battery of claim 12, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
