title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.

14. The method of claim 13, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window.

9. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 8, further comprising a rare earth element substituting part of the metal.
10. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.
11. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 288 degrees C to 312 degrees C.
12. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.

16. The method of claim 15, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
21. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 20, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
22. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 21, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved moisture stability.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and cycle life.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material. The content of SiS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The resulting LLTO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
claims: 1. 2. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 232 degrees C to 253 degrees C.
3. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.45 micrometers to 4.5 micrometers.
4. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 3, wherein devitrification to a Li4P2S6 phase is 5% or less by weight.
5. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the glass phase further contains at least one selected from the group consisting of GeS2, SiS2, LiI, Li2O, and P2O5.

6. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
9. The method of claim 6, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
claims: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.
2. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
3. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a lithium carbonate layer on the surface is removed by polishing in an argon atmosphere.
4. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the dopant is at least one selected from the group consisting of Ta, Nb, W, Ga, and Al.
5. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 10 mol%.
6. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
7. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
8. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
9. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein 0.2 <= v <= 0.35.
10. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ion-conductive solid in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
claims: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.
2. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used.
3. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.
4. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein M is at least one selected from the group consisting of Y, In, Sc, Er, and Yb.
5. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 4, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
6. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
7. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 288 degrees C to 312 degrees C.

8. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.
9. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
10. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
11. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.
12. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
13. The all-solid-state battery of claim 12, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

6. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
claims: 1. title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and method for producing the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
