title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity at a lower cost.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

9. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with LiF is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the sinterability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The LLTO and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

9. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li3YCl6 material. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

11. The positive electrode active material of claim 10, wherein the core particles are secondary particles having an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers.
12. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the dendrite suppression.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
