title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The resulting LATP and LLTO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the high-voltage stability is retained.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with an indium additive. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ceramic ion conductor particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Densified NASICON-type lithium aluminum titanium phosphate ceramic ion conductor sintered with a lithium borate aid and lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a composition represented by Li(1+x)Al(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3, wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.5, and a sintering aid phase comprising Li3BO3 located at grain boundaries in an amount of 1 wt% to 4 wt%. A mother powder prepared by ball milling the calcined phosphate and the borate is pressed into a pellet and sintered at 850 degrees C to 950 degrees C, which is 100 degrees C to 200 degrees C lower than the temperature required without the aid. The liquid borate phase wets the grains during sintering and gives a relative density of 95% or more and an average grain size of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers. The grain boundary resistance is 25% or less of the total resistance and the total ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more. Because the borate phase is oxidation-resistant, the sintered body is stable up to 5.0 V versus Li/Li+ and can be used as a separator facing a high-voltage positive electrode. A lithium battery comprising the sintered body shows improved high-voltage stability and capacity retention.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 30% or less is provided. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the solid electrolyte of claim 10.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The LiF layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
