title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The resulting Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state lithium battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ion-conductive solid shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The Li3N layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved moisture stability.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
claims: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.
2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide is suppressed.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 288 degrees C to 312 degrees C.

8. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
11. The method of claim 8, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

2. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
3. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.9 mol% to 2.7 mol%.
4. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the crystal phase has an average crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm.
5. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.
6. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the glass phase further contains at least one selected from the group consisting of GeS2, SiS2, LiI, Li2O, and P2O5.
7. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers.
8. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

9. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

12. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

2. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more.
3. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
4. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
5. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.
6. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein penetration of lithium filaments along grain boundaries is suppressed.
7. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.2 micrometers to 4 micrometers.
8. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 4 mA/cm2 or more.
9. The negative electrode structure of claim 8, wherein void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed.
10. The negative electrode structure of claim 9, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
11. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the electronic conductivity of the layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less.
12. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
13. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers.
14. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 3.5 wt% to 7.5 wt%.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The LATP and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
