title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.

2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 33% or more.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles.

5. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
6. The method of claim 5, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

7. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
claims: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.
2. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes.
3. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 2, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
4. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

5. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.
6. The method of claim 5, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
7. The method of claim 5, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

8. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1.
9. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a zinc additive. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

2. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 540 degrees C to 570 degrees C.
3. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
4. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.4 mol% to 4.5 mol%.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
7. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 70% or more.

9. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.
10. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

11. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
claims: 1. 2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 2, wherein the coating layer is amorphous as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 66 mol% or more.

7. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
8. The solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.
9. The solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
10. The solid-state battery of claim 9, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
11. The solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

8. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
9. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 200 degrees C.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.
5. The method of claim 4, wherein the solvent is at least one selected from the group consisting of tetrahydrofuran, acetonitrile, ethyl acetate, and 1,2-dimethoxyethane.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.08 wt% or less.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 58 degrees C to 67 degrees C.
9. The method of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 1 micrometers.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the suspension further contains LiCl dissolved therein.
11. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.1 wt% or less.
12. An ion-conductive solid produced by the method of claim 1.
13. The ion-conductive solid of claim 12, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
14. The ion-conductive solid of claim 12, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.

15. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the ion-conductive solid of claim 12.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The LATP and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The LATP and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.15 or less. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LiF, and Li3PS4 material. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The silicon content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
