title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.

A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in anisole with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LLTO material. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
claims: 1. 2. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
3. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 2, wherein a lithium carbonate layer on the surface is removed by polishing in an argon atmosphere.
4. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the dopant is at least one selected from the group consisting of Ta, Nb, W, Ga, and Al.
5. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 3.5 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
6. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5.

7. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tungsten oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
9. The method of claim 7, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

10. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

4. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the substituting element is at least one selected from the group consisting of Sn, Sb, Si, and O.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

7. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 7, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, LATP, and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The LLZO, LATP, and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The resulting LiF and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life during fast charging.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

6. The solid-state lithium battery of claim 4, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.

3. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
4. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
