title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability and sinterability at a lower cost.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the dendrite suppression of the cell.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON solid electrolyte stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. With zirconium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium indium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium indium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A precursor of the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). With germanium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life during fast charging.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

9. The method of claim 7, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved electrochemical window.

5. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 4, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 2 cm3/g or less.
7. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
8. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 7, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
9. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.
10. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the substituting element is at least one selected from the group consisting of Sn, Sb, Si, and O.
11. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 10, wherein the powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity.
12. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 380 degrees C to 430 degrees C.
13. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.5 mS/cm or more.

14. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 4 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The content of Li2O is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

7. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

10. The method of claim 8, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
claims: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more.
2. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mS/cm or more.
3. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
4. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
5. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the H2S generation is measured by a hydrogen sulfide sensor in a sealed chamber of 1 L at 25 degrees C.
6. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

7. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and a silicon source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

10. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
11. The all-solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
claims: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.
2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 104% or more.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 3, wherein the coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 4, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

8. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
9. The lithium secondary battery of claim 8, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
10. The lithium secondary battery of claim 8, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer.
11. The lithium secondary battery of claim 8, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

9. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic.
10. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers.
11. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 200 cycles or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

6. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein 0.19 <= z <= 0.23.

8. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 7, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
9. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 8, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
10. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more.
11. The halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.7 mS/cm or more.
