title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Positive electrode active material with a gradient lithium niobate coating layer whose outer region contains lithium indium chloride
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide with a nickel content of 85 mol% or more and a gradient coating layer having an average thickness of 8 nm to 25 nm. The inner region of the coating layer adjacent to the core consists of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the outer region contains lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) dispersed in the niobate so that the indium content increases continuously from 0 at% at the core to 15 at% to 30 at% at the outer surface. The coating layer is formed by applying a niobium alkoxide solution, heat-treating at 320 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and then applying an alcoholic solution of Li3InCl6 followed by vacuum drying. The niobate inner region blocks the formation of a space-charge layer and the diffusion of nickel into the sulfide, while the chloride-rich outer region, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+ and conductive to lithium ions, lowers the charge transfer resistance with Li6PS5Cl. The coverage is 92% or more and the interfacial resistance after 100 cycles at 4.3 V is 15 ohm cm2 or less. When the sulfide is a glass ceramic, the coated material further improves the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with a gradient lithium niobate coating layer whose outer region contains lithium indium chloride
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide with a nickel content of 85 mol% or more and a gradient coating layer having an average thickness of 8 nm to 25 nm. The inner region of the coating layer adjacent to the core consists of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the outer region contains lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) dispersed in the niobate so that the indium content increases continuously from 0 at% at the core to 15 at% to 30 at% at the outer surface. The coating layer is formed by applying a niobium alkoxide solution, heat-treating at 320 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and then applying an alcoholic solution of Li3InCl6 followed by vacuum drying. The niobate inner region blocks the formation of a space-charge layer and the diffusion of nickel into the sulfide, while the chloride-rich outer region, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+ and conductive to lithium ions, lowers the charge transfer resistance with Li6PS5Cl. The coverage is 92% or more and the interfacial resistance after 100 cycles at 4.3 V is 15 ohm cm2 or less. When the sulfide is a glass ceramic, the coated material further improves the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

3. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The resulting Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. The LLZO and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the sinterability is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved cycle life and simpler handling.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. With hafnium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The LLZO and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With hafnium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
