title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

3. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.
claims: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.
2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide is suppressed.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 380 degrees C to 420 degrees C.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 4, wherein the coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

7. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
8. The method of claim 7, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
9. The method of claim 7, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

10. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
11. The lithium secondary battery of claim 10, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

2. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.
3. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 2, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

4. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
5. The method of claim 4, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

6. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.
7. The lithium secondary battery of claim 6, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The resulting Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

7. The method of claim 6, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A precursor of the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life.
claims: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 12 wt% to 22.5 wt%.
3. The method of claim 2, wherein the suspension further contains LiCl dissolved therein.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein the solvate complex is a tetrahydrofuran solvate of Li3PS4.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed for 6 hours to 72 hours.
9. An ion-conductive solid produced by the method of claim 1.
10. The ion-conductive solid of claim 9, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
11. The ion-conductive solid of claim 10, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.

12. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the ion-conductive solid of claim 9.
13. The all-solid-state battery of claim 12, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

7. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
9. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the solid electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
10. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.
11. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 4.8 V
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
claims: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.
2. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
3. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used.
4. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

5. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.
6. The method of claim 5, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

7. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
8. The solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved high-voltage stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability in contact with lithium.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 96% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the interfacial resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A precursor of the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The binder content is 1 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
