title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The content of GeS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A precursor of the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The resulting Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the cycle life are improved.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state lithium battery. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the solid-state cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the high-voltage stability of the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The content of LiI is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Tin-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Germanium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LATP, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The tensile strength is 1.2 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which indium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.

abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which indium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

10. The moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity.

11. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
14. The method of claim 13, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
15. The method of claim 11, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The LiF layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with an indium additive. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
