title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF and Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sinterability.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Bromine-containing argyrodite solid electrolyte with suppressed lithium chloride impurity and improved moisture stability
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein a = x + y, 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5. Replacing part of the chlorine with bromine expands the lattice and raises the anion disorder on the 4a and 4d sites, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway, while the halogen-rich composition is fired at 460 degrees C to 520 degrees C so that a lithium chloride impurity phase does not precipitate. In an X-ray diffraction pattern measured with CuK-alpha radiation, the ratio of the peak intensity at 2-theta = 34.8 degrees attributed to LiCl to the peak intensity at 30.0 degrees attributed to the argyrodite phase is 0.05 or less. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 7 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, retains 85% or more of the conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, and keeps the argyrodite phase without a glass ceramic by-product. Compared with Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 type conductors, the material gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sinterability of the cell.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

3. The protective layer of claim 2, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.

5. The protective layer of claim 4, wherein the inorganic layer is amorphous.
6. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 140 nm to 300 nm.
7. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 300 cycles or more.
8. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
9. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

10. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
12. The method of claim 10, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

13. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

6. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
9. The method of claim 7, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

10. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
11. The solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The content of LiI is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LLZO material. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. The binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
