title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LiF material. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved high-voltage stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. A precursor of the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Al2O3 inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.

The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the solid-state cell.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a silver additive. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
