title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
claims: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

4. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sintering is hot pressing at a pressure of 10 MPa to 50 MPa.
5. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sintered body has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 500 micrometers.
6. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.
7. The garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

8. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
12. The method of claim 8, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
13. The method of claim 10, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and production method thereof
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and cycle life of the solid-state battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The LLZO, LLTO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li3PS4 material. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
